Coastal wetlands reduce flood damage by slowing storm surge, absorbing wave energy and storing water. Their effect depends on the width of the marsh, the density of vegetation and the duration of the storm, so they lower risk rather than remove it. Engineers increasingly pair them with levees and sea walls.
